What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

RFRed Fox9m ago

Lead with the recommendation; the finding can follow.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

MLMaya Lindqvist3m ago

Was it twice? The log says once, on the 14th.

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

MLMaya Lindqvist5m ago

Two days is optimistic. Last time the same job took a week; say so, or give a range.

The path

RFRed Foxjust now

Walkers need a sign here before the meadow is gone.

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To show text people copy exactly: a command to run, a prompt for an agent, a snippet of code or configuration, a file path.
  • To show output exactly as a tool printed it: an error, a check result, a log.

When not to use

  • For a short name or path inside a sentence: use inline code.
  • For editable text: use cmp-text-field with a textarea.
  • For prose that people read rather than copy.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a quiet well with a hairline edge: for code and prompts on a page or in a panel. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • strong — the dark terminal look on the strong surface: for commands people run, especially on public pages. One strong block per view.
  • flush — no edge, corners or fill, so it sits edge to edge inside a card (for example below a card's own header).
  • compact — less air around the code and a smaller size: for one short command shown under a line of text, such as a step in a list of steps. Usually without a header; combines with nowrap and strong.
  • nowrap — for a terminal: a line never breaks in the middle of a word. A line longer than the block wraps at a space, as a terminal would, and the rest hangs two characters in, under the command after its $, so nothing is cut off at the edge or hidden behind a sideways scroll (which touch screens never show). Only a single word longer than the line breaks. Combines with strong.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-code-block" data-ds="code-block">; add ds-code-block--strong or ds-code-block--flush for those variants. data-ds="code-block" marks the block whose copying component.js adds.
  • Header: <div class="ds-code-block__header"> holding an optional <span class="ds-code-block__title"> (what this is: "Terminal", "Prompt", a file name) and the copy button.
  • Copy button: <button class="ds-code-block__copy" type="button"> with <span class="ds-icon ds-code-block__copy-icon" data-icon="copy"></span>, <span class="ds-icon ds-code-block__done-icon" data-icon="check"></span> and <span class="ds-code-block__copy-label">Copy</span>. After copying, the button gets data-copied, the check replaces the copy glyph and the label reads "Copied" for a moment.
  • Code: <pre class="ds-code-block__code"><code>…</code></pre>. Long lines wrap; nothing is cut off.
  • Prefix (optional): <span class="ds-code-block__prefix">$ </span> before a command; it is shown but never copied.
  • Comment (optional): <span class="ds-code-block__comment"> for comments and output lines, in the muted colour. In a block whose commands carry the prefix, only the prefixed lines are copied, so output is shown but never pasted; in a block without prefixes everything is copied.
  • A copy button outside the block (for example in a Composite's own header) is a cmp-button with its with-copy parts (ds-button__copy-icon, ds-button__done-icon, ds-button__label and its ds-button__sizer spans) and data-ds-copy; this script copies the nearest code block in its container, sets data-copied and changes the words in its [data-ds-copy-label]. That is the one copy pattern every Composite uses; the header's own copy button above is the block's built-in one, because a Basic includes no other component.

Accessibility

  • The copy button is a native button named by its visible label ("Copy"). Its new label ("Copied") is also announced politely, and focus stays on the button.
  • When copying is blocked, the code is selected instead and the label says "Press Ctrl+C" (or "Press ⌘C"), so keyboard and screen-reader users can finish the copy.
  • The code text meets AA on its fill in every variant and theme (text-default on surface-sunken, text-on-strong on surface-strong, text-muted on surface-raised).
  • The prefix is visual only; screen readers read it, so keep it to a single $ or >.

Interaction

  • Hover and focus on the copy button change colour within the quick duration (int-01); focus stays on the button after copying (int-02).
  • Copying keeps the button's size: only the glyph and the word change, for about one and a half seconds (int-03, int-05).
  • On copying, the check cross-fades over the copy glyph and the new words fade in, over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease; going back, the glyph cross-fades back and the words return at once. Nothing else in the block moves. Under the still preset and reduced motion the change is instant (int-04, int-06).

Contract

  • Parts: the block, a box that holds exact text (ds-code-block); an optional header row across its top (ds-code-block__header) with an optional title, a short noun on one line that ends in an ellipsis when it is too long (ds-code-block__title), and the copy button at the header's right end (ds-code-block__copy), which holds a copy glyph, a check glyph that is hidden until copying, and a word, "Copy" (ds-code-block__copy-label); the code, monospaced text whose long lines wrap so nothing is cut off (ds-code-block__code); an optional prefix before each command, such as $ , shown but never copied (ds-code-block__prefix); optional comment and output lines in the muted colour (ds-code-block__comment).
  • States: the block itself has none; its copy button has default; hover (an edge and a raised fill appear and its text turns the default colour); focus (a focus ring around it); copied (the check glyph replaces the copy glyph and the word reads "Copied" for about 1.6 seconds, then both return to default); and blocked, when the device refuses the copy: the code text is selected instead and the word reads "Press Ctrl+C" ("Press ⌘C" on Apple devices) for about 4 seconds, then returns. In every state the button keeps its size.
  • Inputs: activating the copy button (a click, a tap, or Enter or Space while it has focus) copies the code: when the block has prefixed lines, only those lines without their prefix (output is left out); otherwise all of its text. Tab moves focus to the button like any button, and focus stays on it after copying. Pointer hover shows the hover state. A copy button outside the block (a cmp-button marked data-ds-copy, for example in a Composite's header) copies the nearest code block in its container in the same way and shows the same copied and blocked words.
  • Events: puts the copied text on the device's clipboard; tells assistive technology politely "Copied to the clipboard", or, when blocked, "Text selected. Press Ctrl+C to copy it." (⌘C on Apple devices). It raises nothing else to the screen around it.
  • Geometry: the copy button is at least --ds-target-min wide and tall, with --ds-space-2 padding on its sides and glyphs of --ds-icon-size-sm; the header has --ds-space-1 above and below, --ds-space-4 on the left and --ds-space-2 on the right; the code has --ds-space-4 on every side (compact: --ds-space-2 above and below and --ds-space-3 on the sides; strong: --ds-space-2 above) at --ds-text-size-sm (compact: --ds-text-size-xs) in the mono family; the block's corners are --ds-radius-surface and its edge is --ds-border-width. In nowrap, a line wraps only at a space and its continuation is indented 2 characters. The check glyph grows from half size to full size as it appears; nothing turns.
  • Looks: default is a sunken fill with a hairline default-border edge and default text; strong is the strong (dark) surface with on-strong text, no line under the header, and the title, prefix and comments in on-strong muted; flush has no edge, square corners and no fill, taking the card's surface, with muted text; the copy button is quiet muted text with no edge until hover or focus, and copied shows a check and "Copied". See the specimen's default × default, default × hover, default × focus and default × copied cells, and the strong, flush, compact and nowrap rows for the variants.
  • Names: Not applicable: it is self-contained; nothing it holds crosses to another component, and assistive technology reads the button by its words.
  • Focus: it never takes focus on its own; the copy button is one stop in the tab order and keeps focus after copying, while its words change in place.

Content rules

  • Show exactly what to run or paste, with real values or clearly marked placeholders in angle brackets: <project-folder>.
  • One command per line; put the prefix only on commands, never on output.
  • Titles are a noun: "Terminal", "Prompt for this screen", "package.json".
  • Keep explanations outside the block, in the text before it.

Do and don't

  • Do give every block that people copy a copy button.
  • Do use strong for the one command a public page asks people to run, and default everywhere else.
  • Don't put more than one strong block in a view, or a strong block inside a card.
  • Don't truncate code with an ellipsis, or let it run out of sight: let it wrap, and use nowrap when a word broken across lines could be misread.
